bibl.title: Stone archetypes for inlay molds and molded gypsum case from Dionysias / Qasr Qarun temple.
bibl.seg: Paola Davoli & Mustafa Faisal, Stone archetypes for inlay molds and molded gypsum case from Dionysias / Qasr Qarun temple.
bibl.note: Glass inlays are common finds in Egypt and especially in the Graeco-Roman sites. They were used for decoration of funerary furniture starting from the 18th dynasty but became common and widespread from the 26th Dynasty onward. Items decorated with polychrome glass inlays were and still are often found in excavations of temples and tombs, and they are difficult to date if they do not come from well-known contexts, as it happens to many of them housed in museums and collections. Publications and catalogs of glass inlays are frequent, but, on the contrary, the workshops locations and the manufacture techniques and processing are not well known. A series of objects found by the Supreme Council of Antiquities during a cleaning of the temple at Qasr Qarun, ancient Dionysias (El-Fayyum), in 1951 and 1985 are now kept in the SCA General Storehouse in Kom Aushim. Among these objects, there are 15 slabs of limestone used as archetypes for inlays molds used to produce glass inlays applied on temple furniture of the Greco-Roman period, and eight molded plaster probably once decorated with inserted glass inlays.
